about: Chinese SaaS company making human resource management and payroll software for mid-sized and large companies, with employee attendance, scheduling and talent tools on subscription. Based in Shanghai. Revenue comes from per-employee subscriptions and implementation services. B2B with limited consumer awareness. The company sells to enterprises in sectors like retail, manufacturing and services across mainland China, and competes with larger local HR software vendors.

about: San Francisco on-demand staffing marketplace that connects businesses needing flexible workers in warehousing, logistics, retail and light industrial roles with workers ready to take shifts through an app. Revenue comes from a markup on hourly wages. Venture-backed, with thousands of businesses on the platform. B2B and gig-worker focus, with limited consumer awareness. It lets workers pick up shifts on short notice and gets paid through the app, and is competing with firms such as Instawork and Shiftgig.

about: Online job search engine and aggregator, formerly Neuvoo, that collects millions of postings from employers and job boards across more than 70 countries and charges employers on a pay-per-click basis. It is based in Montreal, Canada, and runs country sites. It is known to job seekers online and has some consumer brand awareness, driven by digital advertising. It claims tens of millions of visitors a month. Employers pay to promote jobs, so the brand has been visible mainly through digital marketing.

about: San Francisco job and company review site, where employees post anonymous salaries, interview and company reviews, and employers pay for recruitment advertising and branding tools. Recruit Holdings, owner of Indeed, acquired it in 2018 for about 1.2 billion dollars. Founded 2007. Well-known consumer job-search brand in the US, UK and Europe. Glassdoor operates as a standalone brand within Recruit's HR technology division.

Rival HR is described as a US human resources software company offering a software suite for HR teams, tagged in Crunchbase under career planning and cloud infrastructure. It is based in the Chicago area. The listed funding figure looks unusually large for a company of this type and may be a data error. Likely a B2B software vendor selling to employers on subscription terms. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Chinese online recruitment platform focused on internet and technology jobs, launched in Beijing around 2013. Job seekers browse openings with salary and company details and chat directly with hiring managers. Employers pay for job postings, recruiter tools and resume access. It differentiated from large rivals by specialising in start-ups, software and product roles, and was backed by investors including Zhenfund, DCM, Tencent and Capital Today. Operates across China's main tech hubs. Familiar among young professionals in China but not a mainstream consumer brand, with no international presence.

about: Chinese online recruitment and headhunting platform (Liepin) founded in Beijing in 2011, focusing on mid-to-senior professionals. Employers and headhunters post roles and search resumes, while candidates use the app and website to find jobs and talk to recruiters. Revenue comes from employer subscriptions, recruiter fees and value-added services. Strong market position in white-collar recruiting in China, with advertising across Chinese media. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Well recognised by Chinese professionals, with no international consumer presence.

about: Japanese spot-work matching platform (Timee) that lets people take short shifts at restaurants, retail, logistics and other employers via a smartphone app, often with same-day payment. Founded in 2017, it serves businesses needing flexible labour and workers wanting casual jobs, earning a commission on wages. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange growth market in 2024. Millions of registered workers and tens of thousands of business sites. Strong brand with younger Japanese consumers.

Guanaitong is a Shanghai-based company tagged under employee benefits and human resources, apparently providing corporate welfare, benefit-purchasing and employee-engagement services to Chinese employers, and shown as listed. The input gives no description, so product details, client numbers and scale cannot be confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

TeamLease Services is India's largest staffing and human resources services firm, founded in 2002 by Manish Sabharwal and Ashok Reddy. It places hundreds of thousands of associates with employers in sectors such as retail, logistics, banking and manufacturing, and also offers payroll compliance, apprenticeship and skills-training programmes. Revenue comes from staffing margins and service fees, running to several thousand crore rupees a year. It is listed on the NSE and BSE. Known mostly to HR buyers and job seekers rather than consumers.

LiveHire is a Sydney-based software company, listed on the ASX, that sells a talent-community and recruitment platform to employers, helping them build pools of candidates and rehire workers directly rather than through agencies. Customers are mid-sized and large enterprises in Australia, New Zealand and the US who pay software subscription fees. It was founded around 2012 by Chris Wynne. B2B software with little public profile.

Custom Ecology is a Mableton, Georgia business, formerly known as Stafford Logistics, tagged under human resources, outsourcing and staffing. The input suggests logistics-related staffing or services, but gives no customers, scale or ownership details. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Meta Platforms is a Menlo Park, California social technology company that owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads, plus Reality Labs (Quest headsets, Ray-Ban Meta glasses) and Meta AI/Llama models. It serves over three billion daily users and earns mostly from advertising, with revenue above $160bn. Listed on Nasdaq (META). One of the most recognised tech brands globally, a huge advertiser, and an active partner in sports through Ray-Ban Meta and Meta AI deals. Funding shown reflects debt financing.

Tencent is a Shenzhen-based Chinese technology and entertainment conglomerate, owner of WeChat (over 1.3 billion users), QQ, Tencent Games (Honor of Kings, PUBG Mobile, Riot Games, Supercell), Tencent Cloud, WeChat Pay, Tencent Music and Tencent Video. Revenue is above RMB 600bn. Listed in Hong Kong (0700). Among the world's biggest tech groups, with enormous domestic consumer awareness and sports and esports ties such as NBA digital rights and League of Legends.

Macy's is a New York-headquartered department store chain founded in 1858, operating Macy's, Bloomingdale's and Bluemercury stores, with about 700 locations and a large e-commerce operation, and sponsoring the Thanksgiving Day Parade. Revenue is about $23 billion. Listed on NYSE (M). Customers are mainstream US shoppers. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US. The input lists advertising among its industries.

Out-of-home advertising company, based in New York and with operations in Europe and the US, owning thousands of billboards, airport displays and street furniture and selling the ad space to brands. Listed on the NYSE (CCO), with its European business sold in 2025. B2B brand, though its displays are highly visible and used for sports advertising. Clear Channel sells advertising in airports and city streets, and its customers include brands, sports teams and event promoters.

Bonn-based German telecoms group and Europe's largest operator, owning T-Mobile (with majority control of T-Mobile US), Telekom Deutschland and T-Systems, serving over 250 million mobile customers. Revenue is about EUR 115 billion. Listed in Frankfurt (DTE); the German state is a significant shareholder. Very high consumer brand visibility and extensive sponsorship, including football. Deutsche Telekom employs about 200,000 people, and it sponsors the football club Bayern Munich and runs a large streaming and broadband business.

New York-based audience measurement company, taken private in 2022 by Elliott and Brookfield, providing the TV and digital ratings that are used as industry currency by advertisers and broadcasters. B2B brand, though widely cited in media, including in sports audience reporting. Also provides consumer data to advertisers and retailers worldwide, with offices in more than 100 countries. Nielsen's ratings are used to set advertising prices, and its reports cover sport, music and shopping behaviour worldwide.

New York-based advertising and marketing communications group, owning BBDO, DDB, TBWA, OMD, and, since 2025, Interpublic (McCann, FCB). Customers are large advertisers. Revenue about $17 billion. Listed on the NYSE (OMC). B2B brand, although its agencies handle high-profile sports campaigns. Employs about 75,000 staff and operates in over 100 countries. Agencies include sports marketing and media buying arms. Omnicom's clients include many of the world's largest brands, and the group has roughly 75,000 employees after the Interpublic deal.

Driven Brands is the Charlotte-based owner of automotive service franchises, including Take 5 Oil Change, Meineke, Maaco, CARSTAR, ABRA, Uniban and Fix Auto, with about 5,000 locations in 15 countries. Revenue comes from franchise fees, company-owned stores and car washes, and it is listed on Nasdaq (DRVN), with Roark Capital as the largest shareholder. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. Strong US consumer brand names in car repair.

Warner Bros. Discovery is a US media and entertainment group headquartered in New York, formed in 2022 by the merger of WarnerMedia and Discovery. It owns Warner Bros. studios, HBO and Max streaming, CNN, TNT Sports, Discovery Channel, Eurosport and many other networks, earning from subscriptions, advertising and content licensing. Listed on Nasdaq (WBD) with revenue of about $40 billion and plans to split into two companies. It holds major sports rights, so it is relevant to advertising and F1-style broadcast partnerships.

InMobi is a mobile advertising and consumer technology company, founded in Bangalore in 2007 and now headquartered in Singapore, with products including an ad network, the Glance lock-screen content platform and Roposo. It earns advertising revenue from brands and app developers and has been backed by SoftBank, Kleiner Perkins and others. Funding shown is about $774 million. B2B in advertising, with Glance reaching hundreds of millions of phone users in Asia.

Canada's largest travel loyalty programme, owned by Air Canada and based in Montreal, with millions of members who earn and redeem points on flights, hotels, car rentals and partner spending. Revenue comes from airlines and commercial partners. Consumer loyalty brand with high awareness across Canada.

Marketing analytics and attribution platform for mobile apps, headquartered in San Francisco with Israeli roots (founded 2011). Brands and advertisers use it to measure ad performance and optimise campaigns, paying by subscription. Customers include large consumer apps. Funding about USD 300 million. B2B software with little consumer awareness, though known in advertising.

Out-of-home advertising company based in New York, owning billboards, transit displays and digital screens across the US and Canada, including in Times Square. Advertisers are its customers and revenue comes from selling display space. Listed on the NYSE (OUT). Its displays are widely seen by the public, but the company brand is B2B.

US online betting and affiliate technology company, formerly SharpLink Gaming, which pivoted in 2025 to holding Ethereum as a treasury business. Based in Miami and listed on Nasdaq (SBET). Little consumer brand awareness; mostly known to investors.

about: US industrial real estate investment trust focused on infill warehouse and distribution properties in six major coastal markets such as Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area and New Jersey. Based in Bellevue, Washington and listed on the NYSE (TRNO). Tenants are businesses; no consumer brand.

Data-driven marketing technology firm headquartered in New York, selling a cloud platform that uses AI and consumer data to run email, mobile and ad campaigns for brands. Listed on NYSE (ZETA), founded by David Steinberg. Customers include large retailers and financial firms. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Razor Group is a Berlin-based e-commerce aggregator that acquires and scales third-party sellers on Amazon and other marketplaces, building a portfolio of consumer brands across categories like home, kitchen and pet. It raised large equity and debt financing in 2021-2022 (about $1.1 billion in total). Customers are consumers via Amazon. Brand is largely B2B and investor-facing; its products are sold under many small brands.

about: MFE-MediaForEurope is the pan-European broadcasting group formerly called Mediaset, headquartered in Cologno Monzese near Milan (and incorporated in the Netherlands), operating Canale 5, Italia 1 and Rete 4 in Italy, Telecinco in Spain, and a controlling stake in ProSiebenSat.1 in Germany. Controlled by the Berlusconi family's Fininvest. Listed in Milan and Madrid (MFE). Major consumer TV reach with advertising-led revenue.

Baidu is a Beijing-based Chinese internet and AI company operating China's largest search engine, along with the Ernie AI models, Apollo Go robotaxi service, iQIYI streaming and cloud services. Founded 2000 by Robin Li. Revenue is about 130 billion yuan, largely advertising plus AI cloud. Listed on Nasdaq (BIDU) and Hong Kong (9888). Huge consumer brand in China.

Kantar is a London-based marketing data, insights and analytics company, formerly the research arm of WPP, sold in 2019 with Bain Capital controlling it, and it later sold Kantar Media to H.I.G. Capital. Offers consumer panels, brand tracking and advertising effectiveness measurement. Revenue is around 2 billion dollars. B2B brand known to marketers and agencies, including sports-sponsorship research.

Authentic Brands Group is a New York brand management and licensing company that buys consumer, sports and entertainment brands and licenses them to manufacturers and retailers. Its portfolio includes Reebok, Brooks Brothers, Sports Illustrated, Shaquille O'Neal, Marilyn Monroe, Elvis Presley, Juicy Couture, Ted Baker and Champion's apparel business. Revenue comes from royalties on over 30 billion dollars of retail sales. Founded in 2010 by Jamie Salter, privately held with investors including BlackRock and Brookfield. Portfolio brands are very visible even if the group is not.

RR Donnelley is a Chicago-based commercial printing and marketing services company that prints books, catalogs, labels, direct mail, packaging and financial documents, and offers supply chain and marketing support. Founded in 1864, it was listed on the NYSE (RRD) before being taken private by Chatham Asset Management in 2022 after years of restructuring. Customers are publishers, retailers, banks and consumer brands. B2B service business with moderate name recognition among marketers, little among consumers.

Webuild is Italy's largest construction and engineering group, building large infrastructure such as railways, metros, dams, bridges, roads and airports in dozens of countries, including the Rome Metro, the Snowy 2.0 hydro project in Australia and the Salini Impregilo projects in Africa. Formerly Salini Impregilo, it was renamed Webuild in 2020 and is listed in Milan (WBD) with the Salini family and Cassa Depositi e Prestiti as shareholders. Revenue is above 10 billion euros. Known to governments and business, with modest consumer awareness.

DoubleVerify is a US digital media measurement and analytics software company that verifies ad quality for brand safety, fraud prevention, viewability and suitability. Advertisers, agencies and ad platforms use its tools to track whether adverts appear in safe, real environments, earning revenue from usage-based fees. Founded in 2008 in New York and listed on the NYSE (DV) since 2021, with revenue around 700 million dollars. B2B adtech with strong awareness among marketers and little among the public.

System1 is a US marketing technology and omnichannel customer acquisition company based in Marina Del Rey, California. Its platform uses data and responsive acquisition marketing to connect consumers to search, content and advertising from partners, and it owns brands such as Startpage and MapQuest. It went public through a 2022 SPAC merger with Trebia, and is listed on the NYSE (SST). Low direct public awareness, though its products reach many internet users.

The New York Times Company is a US news publisher headquartered in New York, producing The New York Times, plus The Athletic, Wirecutter, Cooking and the Games (Wordle) brands. Revenue is mostly from digital and print subscriptions (over 11 million subscribers) plus advertising, with annual revenue around 2.6 billion dollars. Founded in 1851, it is listed on the NYSE (NYT) and controlled by the Ochs-Sulzberger family. Globally recognised news brand with an affluent, educated audience, and The Athletic gives it sports reach.

Advantage Solutions is a US sales and marketing services company, based in Irvine, California (the input lists St Louis), providing outsourced sales, merchandising, retail services and experiential marketing to consumer goods makers and retailers. It listed on Nasdaq (ADV) in 2020 through a SPAC merger and has about 70,000 staff. B2B with strong awareness among CPG brands and low among consumers.

Disney Streaming, formerly BAMTech, was the Disney technology unit that powered streaming services such as Disney+, Hulu and ESPN+ and sold video technology to third parties. Based in New York, it was folded into Disney's wider media and entertainment organisation in the early 2020s. Customers are consumer subscribers and advertisers. Owned by Disney (NYSE: DIS). The streaming brands have enormous consumer visibility.

Reliance Jio, now Jio Platforms, is India's largest mobile operator, launched in 2016 by Reliance Industries, with 4G and 5G mobile, JioFiber home broadband, apps such as JioCinema and JioHotstar and enterprise services. Based in Navi Mumbai, with over 450 million subscribers. Backed by Meta and Google, and shareholders including investors such as KKR. Huge Indian consumer brand and a major sponsor of Indian sport.

Multi-Color Corporation is a global manufacturer of label solutions for consumer brands in home and personal care, food and beverage, wine and spirits, healthcare and specialty sectors, making pressure-sensitive, in-mould, shrink sleeve and cut-and-stack labels. It operates dozens of plants across North America, Europe, Latin America, Asia and Australia. Based in Atlanta, Georgia, it was taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2019 after being listed on Nasdaq (LABL). B2B packaging supplier whose labels appear on well-known products but whose name has no consumer visibility.

VerSe Innovation is an Indian regional-language mobile content and technology company, running Dailyhunt (a news and content aggregator in more than a dozen Indian languages) and Josh (a short-video app launched after the TikTok ban in India). It earns revenue from advertising and brand partnerships and serves tens or hundreds of millions of monthly users. Headquartered in Bangalore, Karnataka, founded in 2007 as Eterno Infotech, backed by Google, Microsoft, Qatar Investment Authority, Goldman Sachs and others, with funding of around 1.7 billion dollars. Strong India consumer app brand and a youth audience.

Klaviyo is a Boston-based marketing automation platform that helps e-commerce and consumer brands send email, SMS and push messages using customer data from stores such as Shopify. It earns subscription revenue from over 150,000 customers; ARR passed 1 billion dollars. Founded in 2012 by Andrew Bialecki and Ed Hallen. Listed on the NYSE (KVYO) since its September 2023 IPO. B2B software brand, well known among online merchants and marketers, little general consumer visibility.

Publicis Groupe is one of the world's three largest advertising and communications holding companies, headquartered in Paris. Its agencies and platforms include Leo Burnett, Saatchi & Saatchi, Publicis Worldwide, Starcom, Zenith, Digitas, Razorfish, Epsilon and Sapient, and it acquired data firm Epsilon in 2019. Revenue is around 16 billion euros with about 100,000 employees in 100 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (PUB). Customers are large global advertisers. B2B agency network; Leo Burnett and Saatchi are recognized in the industry but the group has low public awareness.

Outbrain is a New York-based advertising technology company known for content recommendation widgets (the 'Around the Web' links on publisher sites) and for its Teads acquisition in 2024. It earns revenue when advertisers pay to promote content or video across premium publishers and apps. Founded in 2006 in Israel, it listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (OB). After buying Teads, it renamed itself Teads Holding. Customers are brands, agencies and publishers. B2B ad-tech with limited consumer recognition.

Cenomi Centers, formerly Arabian Centres Company, is the largest mall owner and operator in Saudi Arabia, running lifestyle shopping malls such as Hayat Mall and Salaam Mall, leasing space to retailers and offering advertising. It is part of the Cenomi group, backed by Fawaz Alhokair family, and listed on the Saudi Exchange. Based in Riyadh. Revenue is from rents. Strong consumer-facing mall brands, with sponsorship and media assets.

Foundever, formerly Sitel Group, is a global customer experience outsourcing company providing customer service, technical support, sales and digital content moderation by phone, chat and AI, with around 150,000 employees in about 45 countries. Headquartered in Miami, it is owned by the Mulliez family's holding Creadev. Customers are large enterprises such as telecom, tech and retail groups. B2B service brand with little consumer awareness.

Whop is an online marketplace and platform, founded in 2021, where creators and businesses sell digital products, software, courses, paid communities and memberships, with built-in payments, access control and affiliate tools. It serves creators, traders, online entrepreneurs and small digital businesses, and earns a percentage of transactions. The Crunchbase figure of about $478 million in funding looks high for its venture funding, and may include other measures, and no HQ is shown in the data. Popular among online creators, with limited general consumer awareness.

Monotype is a Woburn, Massachusetts typography and design company, long known for Helvetica, Arial and other fonts, and owner of the MyFonts, Fonts.com and Linotype libraries, which license fonts to brands, device makers and software developers. It also provides brand design services. It was a listed company, then taken private by HGGC in 2019 for about $825 million. Customers include Apple, Microsoft and major consumer brands. B2B design supplier, with high recognition in the design community but low consumer awareness.

Magnite is the largest independent sell-side advertising platform, listed on Nasdaq (MGNI), formed from the combination of Rubicon Project and Telaria with later acquisitions of SpotX and SpringServe. Its technology lets publishers, streaming TV services and app owners sell ad inventory automatically to agencies and brands, and it earns a share of ad spend. Revenue is about $600-700 million. Based in Los Angeles, with offices in New York and other cities. B2B advertising technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Brevo, formerly Sendinblue, is a cloud-based digital marketing platform headquartered in Paris, offering email and SMS marketing, marketing automation, CRM, live chat and transactional messaging for small and medium businesses. It has hundreds of thousands of customers worldwide on subscription plans, and has raised about $780 million in funding including a 2021 round led by Bridgepoint. Founded in 2012. B2B software brand with growing marketing profile but little consumer awareness.

BuzzFeed is a New York digital media company, listed on Nasdaq (BZFD), known for viral lists, quizzes, news (BuzzFeed News closed in 2023), and food and lifestyle brands such as Tasty, plus HuffPost and Complex acquisitions. It earns money from advertising, commerce and content licensing, with revenue of a few hundred million dollars. Founded in 2006 and listed via a SPAC in 2021. Large online audience, particularly among younger readers, and a high-profile consumer media brand.

Etsy is a Brooklyn, New York online marketplace, founded in 2005 and listed on Nasdaq (ETSY), where independent sellers sell handmade, vintage and craft goods. It also owns Reverb, Depop and Elo7, and earns revenue from listing and transaction fees, advertising and seller services. It has more than 90 million active buyers, with gross merchandise sales of around $13 billion. Strong consumer brand in the US, UK and Europe, with extensive marketing.

Taboola is a New York-based content discovery and native advertising company, listed on Nasdaq (TBLA), founded in 2007 in Israel, that recommends articles and videos at the bottom of publisher sites such as news outlets and, through its Realize platform, helps advertisers reach audiences. It earns a share of advertising spend and has revenue of about $1.7 billion, and works with thousands of publishers including Yahoo and NBC News. B2B ad technology brand, with limited consumer awareness.

The E.W. Scripps Company is a Cincinnati, Ohio media company, listed on Nasdaq (SSP), that owns about 60 local television stations in over 40 US markets, the ION national broadcast network, and the Scripps News and Court TV brands. It earns revenue from advertising, retransmission fees and network distribution. Founded in 1878 by Edward W. Scripps, it has about 5,000 employees and revenue of around $2.5 billion. Broad national reach through its stations and ION, but a B2B corporate name with low consumer recognition.

Comscore is a Reston, Virginia media measurement and analytics company, listed on Nasdaq (SCOR), providing audience measurement, cross-platform viewership data and advertising effectiveness measurement for TV, digital and streaming. Customers are advertisers, agencies, publishers and broadcasters, who buy data and subscriptions. Founded in 1999. It has had a recapitalisation and has shrunk in size since 2018. B2B data brand, known in advertising and media, with no consumer recognition.

Walnut Creek, California online marketplace for lead acquisition, connecting consumers with sellers of insurance, education and other services (formerly Reply.com). Revenue from lead fees paid by advertisers. Venture-funded with about $166 million. B2B performance marketing brand with low consumer awareness.

Small-cap, with the funding figure of $418 million in the data looking inflated relative to its size. B2B/online media with minimal brand profile.

about: Pattern is a Lehi, Utah-based e-commerce acceleration company that helps consumer brands such as Nike, Lego and Bose sell on Amazon and marketplaces worldwide, offering advertising, logistics and software. Listed on Nasdaq in 2025 (PTRN). Founded in 2013, it employs around 1,500 people, and has revenue of roughly $2 billion. B2B and little brand awareness among consumers.

Unybrands is a Miami, Florida e-commerce company that acquires and grows online consumer brands, including those sold on Amazon, according to the input. Scale, portfolio and funding are not stated. It is a young business with low public awareness at company level. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Bluecore is a New York based retail marketing technology company, offering a platform that uses artificial intelligence to personalise email, mobile and advertising campaigns for e-commerce and retail brands. Customers are retailers, such as large fashion and consumer brands, and it earns subscription fees. Founded in 2013 and venture backed. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Grandstand is a Dublin, Ireland company listed on Nasdaq (GRSD), described in the input as the intelligence layer of sports betting and sports media. It appears to serve betting operators, affiliates and media partners with data and marketing technology. Details of its products, scale and history are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Instacart (now Maplebear Inc., listed on Nasdaq as CART) is a San Francisco grocery delivery and pickup platform in the US and Canada working with thousands of retailers such as Costco, Kroger and Aldi. It earns delivery fees, retailer fees, advertising and enterprise software, with revenue of about $3.5 billion. It went public in 2023. Strong US consumer brand awareness, with advertising-led marketing.

DNEG is a London based visual effects and animation studio, formerly Double Negative, which has won multiple Oscars for visual effects on films such as Inception, Interstellar, Blade Runner 2049, Tenet and Dune. It works for studios like Warner Bros, Netflix and Disney in London, Los Angeles, Vancouver, Mumbai and elsewhere, with thousands of artists. Owned by Prime Focus and investors including Novator and Brookfield. Known in film circles and used in F1 media productions.

Mediawan is a Paris based European audiovisual production and distribution group formed in 2015, which owns a large network of production companies making drama, documentaries and entertainment for streamers and broadcasters. KKR owns a major share. It has strong visibility in the French and European media industry, with only a B2B profile among consumers.

The Brandtech Group is a New York and London marketing technology group that provides generative AI content tools and creative services to brand owners, with units including Pencil, Oliver and Jellyfish, and it is backed by Brandtech's founder Jonathan Hall. It serves many large consumer brands, with thousands of employees. B2B marketing services brand with strong standing in the advertising industry.

about: Tuya is a smart device and Internet of Things platform provider, listed on the NYSE (TUYA), founded in Hangzhou, China, and with a US base in San Jose, California shown here. Its cloud platform and software let brands build smart home devices and apps, powering products from many manufacturers worldwide. Customers are device makers, and it has revenue of around 300 million dollars. B2B with low consumer awareness.

Gannett is a US local and national media company, publisher of USA TODAY and hundreds of local newspapers, with a growing digital marketing services business (LocaliQ). Listed on the NYSE (GCI), it was formed in 2019 when New Media merged with the old Gannett, and was renamed USA TODAY Co. in 2025. Revenue is around $2.5 billion. Large consumer news audience and an advertising-led business, and it hosts sports media content.

Constant Contact is a Waltham, Massachusetts digital marketing platform for small businesses and nonprofits, selling email marketing, SMS, social media tools, websites and e-commerce tools by subscription. It has hundreds of thousands of small business customers, mostly in North America. Founded in 1995, it went public on Nasdaq in 2007, was bought by Endurance International in 2015, and later became part of Clearlake Capital-backed Stagwell-linked ownership; funding shown reflects those deals. B2B with moderate awareness among small business owners.

about: Digital Turbine is an Austin, Texas mobile advertising and app distribution company. Its platforms (Ignite, Aurora, MobileFuse) pre-install and promote apps on Android phones for carriers and device makers, including Verizon, AT&T and Samsung, and sell app install advertising to developers. Revenue is around 500 to 600 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (APPS) after acquiring Mobile Posse, Fyber and AdColony. B2B, with low public awareness and little direct consumer branding.

Dotdash Meredith is a New York digital and print media company that owns brands including People, Better Homes and Gardens, Investopedia, Allrecipes, Southern Living, Real Simple, Verywell and Food and Wine. It generates revenue from advertising, licensing, commerce and subscriptions, reaching about 200 million people a month. Formed in 2021 when IAC's Dotdash acquired Meredith, it is owned by IAC, listed on Nasdaq (IAC), which acquired it fully. Its titles are widely recognized by US consumers.

Foursquare is a location technology company based in San Francisco, with roots as a check-in app founded in 2009. Today it licenses location data, places datasets and developer tools, and sells advertising measurement and analytics under Foursquare Places, Movement and Audience, plus the consumer Swarm and Foursquare City Guide apps. Customers are marketers, mapping and app companies. It merged with Factual in 2020 and has raised about 394 million dollars. It is private. Known brand among tech users, but now mostly B2B.

Ipsos is a Paris-based global market research and consulting group, founded in 1975, providing surveys, polling, brand tracking, advertising testing and public opinion research. It operates in around 90 markets with about 20,000 employees and annual revenue of roughly 2.4 billion euros. Customers are consumer brands, governments and media. It is listed on Euronext Paris (IPS). Its polls are widely cited in news, but it is a B2B firm with little consumer branding.

Lamar Advertising is a Baton Rouge, Louisiana outdoor advertising company that owns and operates billboards, digital displays, transit and airport advertising, and logo signs along highways across the United States and Canada, with over 360,000 displays. Customers are local and national advertisers, who pay to rent space. Revenue is around 2.2 billion dollars. Founded in 1902, it is a real estate investment trust listed on Nasdaq (LAMR). A familiar roadside presence, but a B2B advertiser-facing brand.

Xcel Brands is a New York-based media and consumer products company that owns and licenses fashion and lifestyle brands, including Isaac Mizrahi, Halston, Judith Ripka and C. Wonder, and collaborates with celebrities, selling mostly through licensees and QVC-style television retail and online. Revenue comes from licensing royalties, design fees and direct product sales. It is listed on Nasdaq (XELB). Brands have moderate US consumer recognition, mainly through home shopping.
